name: Grab
description: Grab is Southeast Asia's leading 'super-app': one app for ordering food and groceries (Deliveries), hailing rides and taxis (Mobility) and, increasingly, borrowing and paying (Financial Services), across Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Rides earn the profit today: Mobility is 36% of revenue but its segment adjusted EBITDA ($690M in 2025) exceeds the whole group's ($500M after $368M of regional corporate costs). Deliveries is 53% of revenue and now profitable; Financial Services (loans, digital banks) is small and still loses money but is growing fastest and is where Grab is spending, including a $1.49B deal announced 2026-09-15 to buy 60% of Atome Financial.

businessLines.name: Deliveries
businessLines.how: Commission (take-rate) on the value of each order paid by merchants, plus delivery and platform fees charged to consumers, plus advertising; consumer promotions are netted against revenue.
businessLines.description: Food, grocery and parcel delivery, plus advertising sold to merchants.

businessLines.name: Mobility
businessLines.how: Commission on each fare paid to driver-partners, plus platform fees; the driver, not Grab, owns the vehicle.
businessLines.description: Ride-hailing (cars, motorbikes, taxis), transport and related services.

businessLines.name: Financial Services
businessLines.how: Interest and fees on loans to consumers, drivers and merchants, plus payment and insurance fees; growth tracks the gross loan portfolio, and credit losses are a cost.
businessLines.description: Lending (GrabFin), digital banks ('Digibanks' including Superbank, consolidated since June 2026), payments and insurance.

brands.name: Superbank (Indonesia digital bank)
brands.note: Consolidated from June 2026; the remeasurement gain of $307M boosted Q2 2026 profit

brands.note: 60% for $1.49B cash, expected to close by Q3 2027, remainder to be bought about two years later
